A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Taccel simulator and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. v2's Appendices A–C can be reliably matched to material in v1, distinguishing relocated content from additions.

before.justification: Sections 7–8 report original simulation and physical experiments on tactile fidelity, parallel throughput, object classification, robotic grasping, and articulated-object manipulation.

after.justification: Sections 5–6 retain these original empirical results and add a controlled friction and shear-deformation experiment in Section 5.3.

M1.justification: The ABD-IPC simulator, gel model, kinematic control, tactile-signal generators, and modified DFC grasp objective are retained. Appendices A and C.4 reorganize existing formulations; newly disclosed training details do not establish changes to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds a controlled grasp-and-pull scenario using two bars with different friction and varying indentation, including static and slipping contact. The original shape-testing, mechanical-part classification, four-hand grasping, and articulated-object coverage remains.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains PyBullet, SAPIEN, DiffTactile, Isaac Sim, and the no-ABD variant; Figure 4 retains SAPIEN-IPC. The new shear experiment compares simulation with physical measurements without adding a competing method. Changed SAPIEN-IPC citations do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new shear evaluation specifies 2 mm/s pulling, indentation depths of 0.3–0.5 mm, friction calibration using one trajectory, evaluation on two other conditions, and trajectory L1 error. Additional settings for retained experiments are predominantly newly disclosed details, not evidence that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Figure 3(b) add a focused error and sensitivity analysis of simulated shear trajectories under different friction and loading conditions, testing agreement through sticking and slipping. Existing physics ablations and manipulation case studies remain; Figure A1 redisplays earlier grasp examples.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly discloses averaging five RGB recordings to suppress noise, and Section 6.1 specifies four randomized evaluations per real classification sample. v1 gives neither repetition count. These disclosures do not establish an increase in independent experimental runs.

E6.justification: Figure 3(b) adds six shear-trajectory comparisons with L1 errors of 0.012–0.080 mm and an aggregate of 0.028 ± 0.024 mm. Existing results retain SSIM 0.93, mechanical-part accuracies of 86.50% and 70.94%, the scaling curves, four-hand classification scores, and Tac-Man switch counts.

T1.justification: The Euler–Lagrange expression is corrected: v1 Section 3.2 differentiates the position derivative of L with respect to time, whereas v2 Section 3.2 and Appendix A.2 correctly use the velocity derivative. The remaining IPC/ABD derivations and grasp objectives are retained, largely through relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: accurate integrated tactile simulation, large-scale GPU parallelization, flexible robot-sensor integration, and useful sim-to-real transfer. The additional shear experiment supports the existing precision claim without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new shear results as evidence of fidelity in both static and slipping contact. Its limitations paragraph removes v1's lack of real-time rendering and a GUI, and the engineering gap to an IsaacGym-like platform, without establishing that these limitations were resolved. The computational bottleneck discussion remains.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands reproducibility information across retained experiments: 500 g loading, 200-step simulation scripts, grasp-depth sampling, an 85/15 split, NLL loss, Adam at learning rate 1e-4, 100 epochs, and exponential scheduling. Conversely, the explicit MultiDex-Tac dataset-release statement and pin-pressing acquisition detail disappear. v2 still describes code and documentation release as future work.

R1.justification: v2 removes the GenDexGrasp and ManiSkill3 references, adds Isaac Gym, and corrects SAPIEN-IPC attribution to Chen et al. The explicit MultiDex dataset lineage becomes a generic statement about extending grasping datasets. Broader positioning relative to existing tactile simulators remains stable.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially condensed and reorganized. Robot, sensor, signal-generation, and API material is consolidated into Section 4; detailed derivations, portions of related work, and application details move into Appendices A–C. The abstract and numerous explanatory passages are rewritten, and author information is expanded.

P2.justification: Presentation changes span the paper: Figure 1 becomes a smaller wrapped illustration, Figure 3 incorporates the new shear panel, Figure 4's legend is rearranged, and v1 Tables 2–3 become v2 Table 2(a–b). The original Figure 6 is split between a reduced main-text display and Figure A1. Captions and panel labels are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: The controlled shear/slip validation and Appendix C's concrete collection and training details strengthen the evidence and reproducibility of the existing simulator. These are useful but bounded gains, with the principal results unchanged. Removing explicit rendering/GUI limitations and the named dataset-release statement reduces transparency, but does not outweigh the added validation and documentation.
